applicability.jurisdiction_or_standard_context: UK/Eurocode-oriented portal-frame guidance. Concept guidance only.
not_applicable_to: crane surge design without additional sources

claims.text: The transverse portal frame can be stable in its own plane through frame continuity and bending stiffness, while the building still needs longitudinal stability provisions.
Vertical bracing in side walls commonly carries longitudinal horizontal actions to the ground.
Plan bracing in the roof commonly transfers gable wind forces and roof drag forces to vertical wall bracing.

limitations: This card does not select or size a lateral system.
Portalised bays, crane surge, fire boundary conditions, and expansion joints need additional project-specific modeling.

pages_used: Portal frames: opening description, Vertical bracing, Plan bracing

summary: Portal-frame reasoning should distinguish transverse frame action from longitudinal building stability and explicitly connect roof and wall bracing load paths.
title: Portal Frame Longitudinal And Transverse Stability
